checks.item: backend_from_log reports cpu on a failed GPU init and does not report gpu from misleading text; its C++ test is real
checks.evidence: Mutation: I replaced the failed_prefix with a dummy string in a scratchpad copy. The test then printed 'CHECK failed ... == "cpu" (line 94)' and FAIL, rc=1, so the test does catch it. Probes: an empty log gives cpu, 'no GPU found' gives cpu, 'using  backend' with an empty device gives cpu, and a failure line after a using line gives cpu. The src file was untouched (git status clean). The parser only sees whisper's init log (g_init_log is cleared before init); transcript text and user text cannot reach it.

checks.item: GPU test would fail on a CPU fallback
checks.evidence: test_gpu_service_runs_on_the_gpu_and_transcribes asserts meta['x-compute-backend'].startswith('gpu:') against port 50052, and the backend string comes from whisper's real init log. A CPU fallback gives 'cpu' and the assert fails. The orchestrator's GPU run (log 'compute backend: gpu:CUDA0', 1 passed, VRAM rose about 400 MiB) is consistent with this. I could not run the GPU path myself (no GPU turn), so I am relying on the orchestrator's observation for the actual GPU run; the code and test logic support it.

checks.item: speech-gpu is profile-gated; a plain start does not take the GPU; behavior without a GPU
checks.evidence: `docker compose config --services` gives db, speech. With `--profile gpu` it adds speech-gpu. speech-gpu has a deploy.resources.reservations nvidia device block, uses CUDA 12.6 ubuntu24.04 build and runtime bases (matching the 24.04 gRPC packages in the runtime stage), and GGML_CUDA=ON. On a machine with no GPU, Docker refuses to start it because of the device reservation (an explicit error); if the CUDA binary does run without a GPU, backend_from_log gives 'cpu', so it does not claim a GPU. This meets 'GPU if reachable else CPU, reporting which', with the GPU opt-in because it is a shared resource.

checks.item: tests/conftest.py deselects gpu tests without hiding others
checks.evidence: Collect-only on the contract file: default gives 1/4 collected; -m real gives 2/4 (the two CPU real tests); -m gpu gives 1/4; -m 'real and gpu' gives 1/4. Full default collect: 303/309 with 6 deselected, which is the real and gpu tests only. The check is by exact keyword 'gpu', so tests with 'gpu' only in their names are not affected. pyproject registers the gpu marker, but the Windows-venv run showed an 'Unknown mark' warning only because I overrode addopts/config in my own run.

Against t81-speech-1: an empty stream returned [] with backend cpu; a stream of odd length with random noise returned a list without crashing; phrase + 2s silence + phrase returned 'thursday' twice with ordered, non-overlapping segments; a cancel mid-stream left the service alive and a following request transcribed correctly. docker logs held only the one start-up line and no 'budget' or 'thursday' text (grep count 0).

Both base images are pinned by tag, and ubuntu:24.04 is pinned by digest in the build log. whisper.cpp is pinned by tag v1.7.6 (a note, not a failure). The model is pinned by the HF revision hash 5359861c... and verified with sha256sum -c.

No legacy/ or .env files in the diff. The HEAD~1 diff touches only speech/, docker-compose.yml, pyproject.toml and the two test files. No test was weakened; test_core.cpp and test_speech_contract.py only gained tests.
